title: Most children climb on and off a couch or chair by about 18 months
summary: CDC says most children, 75 percent or more, climb on and off a couch or chair without help by 18 months.
body: CDC's milestone page for 18 months lists, under movement, climbs on and off a couch or chair without help. The page says developmental milestones are things most children, 75 percent or more, can do by a given age. It also says the Learn the Signs materials are not a substitute for a standardized, validated developmental screening tool. A child who is not climbing yet is not given a diagnosis by this list. The page says to talk with a doctor if a milestone is missing, a skill is lost, or something else worries the family. Climbing is why furniture that can tip matters. The anchor advice is the CPSC card, not a medical label.

sources.title: Milestones by 18 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Reviewed 16 May 2026. Milestone means most children (75 percent or more), not every child, and the page says the materials are not a screening tool.
